objectives: Read familiar CVC words accurately by blending known phonemes.
Notice first, middle and final sound differences in CVC words.
Build early automaticity through short, accurate repeated reading.
concepts: Repeated reading of familiar words can build automaticity.
A changed phoneme can change the whole word.

definitions.definition: Reading accurately and smoothly with appropriate automaticity for the learner's stage.
Recognising a familiar word quickly with little conscious effort after it has been accurately learned.

workedExamples: s-a-t → sat; compare sat with mat by first sound
tap → change first sound /t/ to /m/ to make map
commonMistakes: Guessing from a picture instead of decoding.
Rushing and replacing the final sound.
Treating speed as more important than accuracy.
Failing to reread after an error.
keyTakeaways: Check the changed sound when words look similar.
revisionPoints: First, middle and final sounds all matter.

basic: Read familiar CVC word cards accurately.
conceptual: Compare CVC words by first, middle and final phonemes.
application: Correct a misread CVC word by checking its graphemes.
higherOrderThinking: Diagnose why a learner confused two visually similar CVC words.
Choose a practice sequence that builds accuracy before speed.
mixedReview: Blend, compare, correct and reread familiar CVC words.

formulaOrFactBank: Fluency = accurate decoding + repeated familiar reading + increasing automaticity
mistakeBasedRevision: If the final sound changes, reread the whole word after correcting it.
If a learner guesses, return to grapheme-by-grapheme decoding.
weakTopicRevision: Practise short sets of familiar CVC words, repeating only words that were read inaccurately.

activities.name: CVC word ladder
steps: Change the first sound to make sat.
Change the final sound to make sap or map when the grapheme is known.

activities.name: Accuracy reread
steps: Read five familiar CVC words slowly.
Mark any word that needs correction.
Decode and reread only the missed words.
Read the full set again smoothly.

outcomes: Learner reads at least 8 of 10 familiar CVC words accurately.
Learner identifies first, middle and final phoneme differences in familiar CVC words.
Learner rereads corrected words accurately and more smoothly.

questions.question: Which word can be read by blending /m/ /a/ /t/?
Which word has short /a/ in the middle?
What is a good way to read an unfamiliar CVC word?
options: Look at each sound and blend them
Say any word that looks similar

questions.question: Which pair has the same middle sound?
Which pair begins with the same sound?
Which pair ends with the same sound?
What helps fluent reading most at this stage?
options: Accurate repeated reading of familiar CVC words

questions.question: A learner reads 'mat' as 'map'. Which part should they check?
Which word can be made by changing the first sound in 'sat' to /m/?
Which word can be made by changing the final sound in 'mat' to /p/?
Why should a learner reread familiar CVC words?
options: It removes the need to blend

questions.question: Which sequence supports careful CVC reading?
options: Look → sound out → blend → read smoothly
Read the last letter only → guess
Spell a different word → move on

questions.question: What should a learner do after reading a CVC word incorrectly?
options: Look back at each grapheme, blend again and reread
